$comment: These sRGB values are implementation choices visually matched to the supplied box
The WPF resource dictionary (src/GoldenTicket.Desktop/Theme/Palette.xaml) and any future
PWA custom properties are generated from this file; a test asserts they agree.

Parchment.role: Cream box background; main window and page surfaces

Paper.role: Light paper highlights; raised cards, dialogs, text on dark surfaces

AgedPaper.role: Warm map tones; grouped panels and selected-row background

Burgundy.role: Red title lettering; primary actions and prominent headings

BurgundyHover.role: Deeper title shading; primary-action hover and pressed

AntiqueGold.role: Title edging; dividers, ornaments, restrained story accents

Ink.role: Dark illustration outlines; primary text and strong boundaries

SecondaryInk.role: Sepia map lettering; secondary text and meaningful input borders

RailBlue.role: Blue clothing and box accents; links, secondary actions, keyboard focus

RailCharcoal.role: Locomotive metal; camera surround and opaque privacy curtain

Forest.role: Green illustration details; success icon paired with explicit text

$comment: DESIGN 4.8: gameplay colours are a separate encoding from the decorative palette.
A burgundy button is not the red player's identity. Each is always paired with a seat
name and a redundant symbol so colour is never the only indicator.

contrast.$comment: Calculated in DESIGN 4.8 for the opaque sRGB pairs. Project targets: 4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 essential boundaries.
